cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ, is wrapping up the letter he, Silvanus and Timothy sent to the church of the Thessalonians. He just told them the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, so encourage and build one another up. Now, at the very end, he's got a LIST, friend, and every line on it is short and every job on it is BIG.

cards.question: Paul opens his final instructions with a request. Who does he ask the brothers to acknowledge?

answers.text: Those who work hard and care for them
Those who have believed the longest
Those who give the most to the church

cards.text: Paul says, "In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another." That last line takes three seconds to read and a LIFETIME to do, friend.

cards.question: Paul gives different people different care. He urges the brothers to admonish the unruly and to ___ the fainthearted.
Paul tells the brothers to be patient with each other but not with outsiders.
Now the hardest one on Paul's list. Somebody does you wrong, and your thumbs are ALREADY typing the reply in the group chat. What does Paul tell the brothers to make sure of?

answers.text: That no one repays evil for evil
That the leaders settle it quickly

cards.text: Instead, Paul says, "Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people." Then he goes rapid-fire, short commands, like a coach yelling from the sideline with two minutes on the clock.

cards.question: Paul's rapid-fire list opens with two short commands about joy and prayer. Which two?

answers.text: Rejoice at all times and pray without ceasing
Rejoice on good days and pray every morning
Rejoice in private and pray in public

cards.question: Paul says giving thanks in every circumstance is God's will for the brothers in Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Paul says not to extinguish the Spirit and not to treat prophecies with contempt. Friend, you don't toss the WHOLE batch over one weird-looking cookie.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers not to treat prophecies with contempt. What does he say to do instead?
After testing everything, Paul says to hold fast to what is good but to avoid only the worst kinds of evil.

cards.text: Then Paul's instructions turn into a prayer: may the God of peace Himself sanctify them completely. Completely, friend, not a touch-up, and trust me, I know a little something about getting made new.

cards.question: Paul prays that their entire spirit, soul and body will be kept blameless at the ___ of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul says someone is faithful, and He will do it. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Brothers, pray for us as well." He also tells them to greet all the brothers with a holy kiss, and if I tried that, friend, all you'd get is a face full of MUSTACHE.

cards.question: Paul charges the brothers before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.

cards.text: And Paul signs off: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you." Short, sweet and sealed, baker, just like a cookie box ready to go.

findings.problem: The card links two things with 'so': the Day of the Lord coming like a thief in the night, therefore encourage one another. In the text, the 'Therefore' of 5:11 follows 5:9-10 (God did not appoint us to wrath but to obtain salvation, so that we may live together with Him). It does not follow the thief image in 5:2. The card adds a connection the text doesn't make.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says 'every line on it is short.' That isn't true of this list. 5:12 and 5:23 are long sentences. Only 5:16-22 are short.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: No card tells 'help the weak' from 5:14. Cards 4 and 5 cover admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted and be patient with everyone, but one of the four groups Paul names is left out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Rejoice at all times and pray without ceasing', uses the well-known Bible phrase 'without ceasing.' The wrong answers use plain modern phrasing ('on good days', 'every morning', 'in private'). The right answer sounds more like the Bible and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card says Paul's instructions 'turn into a prayer.' The text gives a 'Now may the God of peace…' blessing and doesn't call it a prayer.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: The question says 'Paul prays that their entire spirit, soul and body will be kept blameless.' 5:23 says 'may your entire spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless' and doesn't call it a prayer.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: The question writes 'He will do it' with a capital H. That marks the subject as God and rules out both wrong answers ('The leaders among them' and 'Paul and those with him') before the baker chooses.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the letter is from Paul, Silvanus and Timothy. After that, every card says 'Paul says' or 'Paul asks', even where the text says 'we ask you' (5:12), 'we urge you' (5:14) and 'pray for us' (5:25). Only 5:27 uses 'I'.
findings.question: In a letter from more than one sender, can Papa Dorin say 'Paul says' for the 'we' lines, or should those lines name all the senders or keep the 'we'?
